page.title: Best 240V Portable Power Station (2026): Split-Phase Picks Compared
page.desc: The OSCAL PowerMax 6000 gives 6,000 W of 240V split-phase from one box. Two Mango Power E units give 7,066 Wh at 240V for less per kWh. Prices checked 2026-11-14.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best 240V portable power station is the OSCAL PowerMax 6000 ({buy:oscal-powermax-6000-3600wh-240v}): 120/240V split-phase from one box, with 6,000 W continuous, 7,200 W surge and 3,600 Wh. The most common failure is a well pump that won't start, so compare your pump's starting watts with that 7,200 W surge figure, not its running watts. For outages that last days, two Mango Power E units joined by Mango's mSocket Pro hub ({buy:mango-power-e-3533wh}) give 7,066 Wh and 6,000 W at 240V for $2,847. That's about $403 per kWh, against $461 for the OSCAL.

All prices are from each maker's US store on 2026-11-14. A 240V station has to make two synchronized 120V legs. A big 120V-only unit won't run a 240V dryer, well pump or central air, however many watts it has. For the lightest single box, the BLUETTI Apex 300 ({buy:bluetti-apex-300}) gives 3,840 W at 120/240V and 2,764.8 Wh from one 83.8 lb unit.

cells.boxes: 2 units of 100.1 lb, plus the hub

rows.model: 2× Growatt HELIOS 3600 + Double Voltage Power Hub

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Start-up surge. This was the complaint we saw most. Well pumps and compressors draw several times their running watts for a second or two, and a station that can't supply that shuts off. OSCAL lists 7,200 W of surge for the PowerMax 6000, and StorageReview lists 7,680 W for the Apex 300. Each Mango Power E is rated for 4,500 to 4,800 W for 10 seconds.
  • Not true split-phase. Forum answers keep pointing out that you can't wire two ordinary 120V stations into 240V. The units have to be built to stay in sync. Every setup in the table is.
  • No wall charging while running 240V. One DIY Solar forum owner called this a deal-breaker for long outages. Mango's manual says to unplug both units' wall-charging cables before you connect the mSocket Pro, so plan to recharge between 240V runs.
  • Weight. Each Mango Power E weighs 100.1 lb. The Gadgeteer called it a beast to move around, even with its wheels. StorageReview called the 83.8 lb Apex 300 a two-person job.
  • Extras add up. Mango's 3,000 W charging cable is $79 and the mSocket Pro is $249. Growatt's pairing hub is $139. A transfer switch or interlock to feed your house panel is another cost, and it needs an electrician.

Which one by need

  • One box, most power for the money: OSCAL PowerMax 6000, at $1,659.99 for 6,000 W and 3,600 Wh. The only add-on pack we found on OSCAL's store, the BP3600 Pro (made for the Pro models), was sold out on 2026-11-14.
  • Multi-day outages at 240V: two Mango Power E units and the mSocket Pro give 7,066 Wh for $2,847. Add one expansion battery per unit ({buy:mango-power-e-expansion-battery}) and you get 14,132 Wh for $5,045, about $357 per kWh. Mango covers the battery cells for 10 years and other parts for 5. Mango's store also lists a 240V Power Kit at $2,599. Check what it includes before you buy.
  • Lightest single box: BLUETTI Apex 300, at $1,499 for 2,764.8 Wh and 3,840 W from a NEMA 14-50 outlet. Add a B300K pack to reach 5,529.6 Wh ($2,599 as a bundle).
  • Two separate stations you can also use apart: two Growatt HELIOS 3600 units with the $139 Double Voltage Power Hub give 7,372 Wh for $3,317.

Not recommended

  • A big 120V-only station for a 240V load. More watts don't change the voltage.
  • Two stations joined with a homemade cord when they aren't sold as a split-phase pair.
  • The Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus (3,840 Wh, 6,000 W, L14-30) for now: Anker's US store showed it sold out on 2026-11-14.

notes: Query choice: Mango Power's US store (mangopower.com, ships free to the contiguous US) sells the Mango Power E (3,533 Wh, 3,000 W, $1,299), an expansion battery ($1,099), the mSocket Pro 240V hub ($249) and plug-in solar kits. In a single-unit 3.5 kWh comparison the Mango loses on price to the OSCAL PowerMax 3600 SE ($1,199 for 3,600 Wh / 3,600 W) and the FOSSiBOT F3600 Pro (about $1,159, maker page, unverified). Plug-in solar is already well covered, and Mango's kit ($2,698 for 1,200 W) doesn't win on price, so I dropped it. For '240v portable power station', the top results are mostly an Anker collection page, brand blogs, retail listings and generic roundups. There Mango honestly wins the multi-day segment. Cost per kWh at 240V from maker stores on 2026-11-14: Mango pair + mSocket Pro $403 ($357 with two expansion batteries), Growatt pair + hub $450, OSCAL PowerMax 6000 $461, Apex 300 + B300K $470, Apex 300 $542. OSCAL leads the page because it's the single-box value (6,000 W, 7,200 W surge, 3,600 Wh, $1,659.99). Pain points from about 14 sources read: start-up surge for well pumps and compressors (5: backuppowerhub, eco-living guide, solar-electric forum, Mike Holt, generatorchecker); true split-phase vs two plain 120V units (4: Mike Holt, solar-electric, OUKITEL blog, generatorchecker); weight (3: Gadgeteer, Solar Lab, StorageReview); app weakness (3: Gadgeteer, Solar Lab, Trustpilot); no wall charging during 240V output (2: DIY Solar thread, Mango mSocket Pro manual); extras cost (2: StorageReview, Solar Lab). Segment winners: one box = OSCAL PowerMax 6000; multi-day at 240V = Mango Power E pair + mSocket Pro; lightest single box = BLUETTI Apex 300. Not verified, so kept off the page: (1) The contents of Mango's '240V Power Kit' ($2,599, in stock). The listing says '7-14kWh' and '240V output', so it is probably two units plus the mSocket Pro, but every product-page read returned HTTP 429. If it is confirmed, the Mango cost falls to $368 per kWh and the kit should get its own record. (2) The 240V receptacle type on the mSocket Pro and the OSCAL PowerMax 6000 (one blog says the OSCAL has an L14-30R). (3) Whether a Mango pair can solar-charge in 240V mode. (4) The OSCAL PowerMax 6000 weight (reviews say 101.4 to 102 lb). (5) FOSSiBOT F3600 Pro 240V support. (6) EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3's current price (retailer snapshots ranged $2,499 to $3,499; the maker page returned 429). (7) Mango E pass-through: the manual describes it in backup mode, while The Solar Lab's 2023 review said there was none, and no switchover time is published. The warranty split (10 years on cells, 5 on the BMS and other parts) and the 30-day return terms come from Mango's own warranty and return pages as quoted in search results. Those pages returned 429 when fetched. Codes: Awin listed none, and I couldn't load Mango's homepage to check for a site banner code (429), so codes is empty.
